# Intra-cluster replication transfer billing

# Intra-cluster replication transfer billing — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Intra-cluster replication transfer billing. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Definitions

- [statement] Keeping transfers within the same provider and region is an Atlas cost-saving recommendation. Apply it to replica placement only after checking availability and recovery requirements; colocating application traffic alone does not remove the separate replication paths that a distributed database requires. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs.md · keywords: Intra-cluster replication transfer billing · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/cost-saving-config.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/replication.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/high-availability.md

## Structure and components

- [statement] For Atlas Infinite, data replicated within the managed storage layer does not count toward data transfer costs. Other transfer still follows Atlas transfer billing. The documentation labels Infinite Public Preview and warns that its behavior and documentation may change. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/atlas-infinite-costs.md

## How it works

- [statement] An Atlas customer on AWS re:Post reported same-region outbound volume rising from 955 TB to 1,997 TB and difficulty identifying transfer detail in Marketplace CUR records. The thread does not establish replication as the cause; its explicitly unreviewed AI-generated answer must not serve as a validated diagnosis. (low confidence) — https://repost.aws/questions/QU_D2a7kIlTJORpJCk7YJFdQ/data-transfer-costs-spike-for-mongodb-atlas

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Estimate replication transfer by enumerating actual communication paths, their metered byte volumes, and the provider/source/destination pricing rules. Atlas's location-dependent billing and AWS's explicit same-AZ versus cross-AZ peering distinction support this path-based method; do not assume AWS peering line items describe Atlas's internal replication paths. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs.md · keywords: Intra-cluster replication transfer billing · also: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/demystifying-amazon-vpc-peering-charges/, https://gd-mrng.github.io/engineering-blog/344-the-cost-of-data-transfer-architecture-decisions-and-network-egress
- [statement] Model topology and traffic volume together when comparing deployments: extra replication destinations can add metered paths even when the stored logical dataset is unchanged. The economic distinction is traffic crossing chargeable boundaries, rather than dataset size alone. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs.md · keywords: Intra-cluster replication transfer billing · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/cost-saving-config.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/replication.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/high-availability.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Atlas documents chargeable node-to-node transfers within a cloud region and across regions; one cluster is therefore not a blanket exemption from transfer billing. Multi-region clusters can have higher transfer costs depending on region placement and deployment size. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs.md · keywords: Intra-cluster replication transfer billing · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/cost-saving-config.md
- [statement] Atlas always compresses intra-cluster communication. Enabling driver compression affects the client-server path; it does not newly enable compression for replication traffic already compressed by Atlas. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs.md · keywords: Intra-cluster replication transfer billing · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/cost-saving-config.md
- [statement] AWS VPC-peering pricing is supporting infrastructure context, not an Atlas replication invoice formula: AWS describes both inbound and outbound peering usage, whereas Atlas documents free incoming cluster transfers on AWS. Applying a generic two-sided AWS rate directly to an Atlas invoice can misstate the charge. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/demystifying-amazon-vpc-peering-charges/ · keywords: Intra-cluster replication transfer billing · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs.md
- [statement] A private path does not universally eliminate transfer charges: AWS states that same-AZ VPC peering transfer is free while cross-AZ and cross-region VPC peering transfer incurs charges. This is an AWS networking rule, not proof of a particular Atlas replication invoice rate. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/demystifying-amazon-vpc-peering-charges/
